Sandbox_RD_SeasonName_tooltip: The folder name for everything this server records. Set it before the first boot, then change it by hand whenever you wipe the world - renaming it is the only thing that starts a new season. Nothing is automatic: records always go to the folder you name here, so if you wipe WITHOUT renaming, the new world's records are added to the old season's folder and the two get mixed together. The server warns you in the console and on screen if it spots that, but it will not change anything for you. Letters, digits, dash and underscore only; anything else becomes a dash.
Sandbox_RD_Debug_tooltip: Print [RFTDCore] diagnostic traces to the console. Leave off for normal play.
Sandbox_RD_DeathCaptureEnabled_tooltip: Records player deaths server-side. Kill switch: the capture hook fires for every character in the world (players, zombies, animals), so if a horde-night performance problem is ever traced here, turn this off and report it.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicRingSegments_tooltip: How many segments each rotating forensic log stream keeps before the oldest is overwritten. Disk ceiling per stream is roughly segments x segment lines x 200 bytes; the default 8 x 20000 is ~40 MB.
Sandbox_RD_ForensicSegmentLines_tooltip: How many lines a forensic segment holds before rolling to the next one. Line-counted rather than byte-counted; after an unclean restart the counter can be up to 500 lines stale, which is expected and harmless.
Sandbox_RD_CmdRelayEnabled_tooltip: Streams inbound client commands to staff consoles as they happen - the Console tab of the Dragonfly panel. A WATCH feature, not a block: the engine has already accepted a command by the time any mod is told about it, so nothing can be refused here. OFF by default because client commands are a firehose (every inventory move, every action sync, from every player). Armed, staff receive ONE batched packet per second, capped at 40 commands per window, and any overflow is reported in the feed rather than silently dropped. Command arguments are NOT sent - those stay in the rotating 'guardian' forensic log, which is the searchable record.
Sandbox_RD_CmdRelayScope_tooltip: Which senders reach the console while the feed is armed. 'Non-staff only' is the default and the useful setting: a privileged command from an account that holds no staff capability is the thing worth seeing, and it keeps your own admins' routine traffic out of the way. 'Staff only' audits what your admins did. 'Everyone' is for debugging and will be loud on a busy server.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeEnabled_tooltip: Measures what the network actually costs: server-to-client sends, client-to-server commands, and global ModData broadcasts (weighted by player count, because one blob is sent to every connection). Writes a top-offenders report to the rotating 'wire' forensic log. OFF by default because arming it wraps engine send functions that every mod on the server uses - turn it on to hunt a bandwidth problem, then turn it back off. Sizes are estimates for ranking offenders, never exact byte counts.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeDumpSeconds_tooltip: Seconds between top-offender reports while the probe is armed. Shorter intervals catch brief spikes but write more log lines; the counters reset after each report.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeTopN_tooltip: How many of the heaviest traffic sources each report lists, ranked by total estimated bytes. Everything is still counted - this only limits how much is written down.
Sandbox_RD_WireProbeOversizedKB_tooltip: A single payload estimated above this size is reported immediately instead of waiting for the next interval. Capped at two alerts per source per interval so one misbehaving mod cannot flood the log.
